+### ADR-0037
+
+**Embedded host composition**
+
+- **Status:** Approved.
+- **Context:** ADR-0004 requires `AddIskender(...)` embedding with the container's pipeline contracts and no global service ownership, and ADR-0031 keeps `Iskender.Hosting` from reaching infrastructure and management assemblies, but no ADR said how a host composes modules, where Iskender's configuration comes from in a host that has its own, or when it is validated. [04](04-technology-stack-and-deployment.md) left the exact public API to a spec, and ISK-0002 left `Iskender.Hosting` outside the compatibility harness.
+- **Decision:** A host calls `AddIskender(options => ...)` on its own `IServiceCollection` and maps Iskender with `MapIskender(prefix)`, one route group per call, whose request bootstrap creates each request's `GatewayExecutionContext`. Each infrastructure assembly offers one explicit registration method, which adds a `CompositionModule` from `Iskender.Domain.Ports` naming its sections and required modules. Registrations come in any order, and no assembly is scanned. Iskender reads only the base and overlay documents named in `IskenderOptions`, and the `ISKENDER__` variables only when the host opts in, never the host's `IConfiguration`, and its environment name is set only in the options, unset and production-grade by default, never derived from the host's. Registration reads and opens nothing. Configuration is validated once per container when the host starts, and a rejected configuration, an unreadable document, or a missing registration fails the host's start with a `hosting.*` code. When coordination is composed, start-up starts the data plane's single-instance guard and runs the capability check once, and a refusal is logged but does not fail start. Iskender adds no middleware, startup filter, exception handler, authentication scheme, logging provider, exporter, or fallback route outside its groups, registers no service a host owns, and keeps no state in a static field outside the classes a reflection scan allows. `Iskender.Hosting` is the public contract `hosting`, version 1, under the compatibility harness, and exposes no `Iskender.Domain` type. The infrastructure registration methods and the seam types stay embeddable and prerelease under ADR-0030. The hosting sample lives under `samples/` with a `sample` role, which is not packable. Three `hosting.*` codes raise `core-contracts` to version 5, and events 6001 to 6003 are written under the category `Iskender.Hosting`. The current hosting contract, linked from the Module boundaries section of [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md) and first published by ISK-0006, holds the exact rules, and the current module dependency rules contract holds the roles and edges.
+- **Rationale:** Explicit registration per assembly keeps `Iskender.Hosting` free of infrastructure edges and loads only what the host asked for. Reading only named documents, with an explicit environment name, means the host's own settings can neither change Iskender's configuration nor relax its production defaults. Validating at host start lets the host log and handle the failure, and keeping all state in the container lets two hosts share a process.
+- **Consequences / trade-offs:** A missing registration is found when the host starts, not when the container is built. Composition start-ups run after the server starts, so a request in between finds the coordination gate fail-closed. Telemetry instruments stay process-wide, so two containers' measurements are reported together. An endpoint in an Iskender group cannot take `GatewayExecutionContext` as a handler parameter. The registrations need `AddIskender(...)`, which the control-plane host must not reach, and `CompositionRegistration.Add` is in `Iskender.Infrastructure`, which `Iskender.Management`, provider adapters, and `Iskender.Policy.Sdk` may not reference, so each of those needs a contract revision before it can compose this way. ISK-0006 composes the ISK-0004 and ISK-0005 adapters into embedded hosts, so ADR-0036's note that ISK-0007 composes the coordinators now covers the container hosts only.
+- **References:** [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md), [04](04-technology-stack-and-deployment.md), [05](05-identity-security-and-privacy.md), [17](17-master-spec-inventory.md).
